name: Herod
overview: The Scriptures reveal Herod as a complex figure marked by moral failure and political ambition, particularly seen in his unlawful marriage to Herodias, his brother's wife, which John the Baptist boldly condemned (Matthew 14:3-4; Mark 6:17). Herod Antipas, the tetrarch of Galilee, is portrayed as a ruler troubled by the ministry of Jesus and the resurrection rumors of John the Baptist, whom he had beheaded (Mark 6:16; Luke 9:7). These passages highlight Herod's tyranny and the tension between earthly power and divine authority during the time of Christ.
